title: Three Somerset villages get share of £50m flooding defence fund - BBC

 Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Rural villages get share of £50m flood defence fund
 13 minutes ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Daniel Mumby Local Democracy Reporting Service Press Association Parts of Somerset are routinely hit by severe flooding A trio of rural villages have secured a share of £50m from central government to help combat flooding.
 The Three Villages Flood Group (3VFG), which covers Ashington, Chilton Cantelo and Mudford near Yeovil in Somerset, said it is one of the groups benefitting from £10m of the funding.
 The Department for the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra) provided funding in early-June for "flood resilience" projects in the aftermath of Storm Chandra, which caused significant disruption across Somerset throughout the winter.
 Somerset Council has been working with the Environment Agency (EA), the Somerset Rivers Authority (SRA) and others to determine which projects the money will be spent on.

 Kay Mackenzie is chair of the Three Villages Flood Group The three villages are one of two communities (the other being Ruishton, near Taunton) which form the pilot phase of the My Community programme.
 They have been allocated £10m of the £50m funding for improvements - which are to be agreed with local residents.
 Chairman of 3VFG Kay Mackenzie said: "We're pleased that our three villages have been selected for the first phase.
 "People here know how flooding affects our homes, roads, farms and businesses.
 "This gives us an opportunity to bring that local experience together with the expertise of partner organisations, and to explore practical ways to make our communities more resilient."
 Additional capital projects due to take place in Somerset include improvements along the River Tone and upgrades to Firepool Weir in Taunton, and the replacement of Vinney Bridge near Bridgwater.
 Thee will also be more dredging and maintenance carried out as part of a previously-agreed programme.
